precepts.text: Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing and said in his heart, then will I slay my brother Jacob; the refusal in Numbers 20 goes back to this.
precepts.point: The hatred is perpetual, everlasting, never ending. The forefather's hatred showed in Numbers 20 and it shows to this day in the nation of Edom still rejecting Israel; it will not stop until Christ stops it, and Israel's part is to repent and come back to the lost statutes and commandments.

note.label: Numbers 20: Strife at Meribah and Edom's Refusal

precepts.why:
Israel asked only to pass through on the highway, paying for any water, and Edom said, “Thou shalt not go through”, and came out with much people and a strong hand. Why so harsh against a people asking only to pass through? That hatred stands from something.

“And Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing wherewith his father blessed him: and Esau said in his heart, The days of mourning for my father are at hand; then will I slay my brother Jacob.” Genesis 25 through 27 is the start of the two nations: Israel was given the birthright and the kingdom while Esau was rejected, and Esau purposed in his heart to slay his brother.

The refusal in Numbers 20 goes back to this. The forefather's hatred showed when Edom came out against Israel with the sword, and it shows to this day in the nation of Edom still rejecting Israel.

precepts.text: Thou hast had a perpetual hatred, and hast shed the blood of the children of Israel; perpetual means everlasting, never ending.
precepts.point: The hatred is perpetual, everlasting, never ending. The forefather's hatred showed in Numbers 20 and it shows to this day in the nation of Edom still rejecting Israel; it will not stop until Christ stops it, and Israel's part is to repent and come back to the lost statutes and commandments.

note.label: Numbers 20: Strife at Meribah and Edom's Refusal

precepts.why:
Edom “refused to give Israel passage through his border”, and the Lord names what that is: “Because thou hast had a perpetual hatred, and hast shed the blood of the children of Israel by the force of the sword in the time of their calamity, in the time that their iniquity had an end.”

Perpetual means everlasting, never ending. The hatred that met Israel at Edom's border is the same hatred that sheds the blood of the children of Israel by the sword in the time of their calamity, and it shows to this day in the nation of Edom still rejecting Israel.

It will not stop until Christ stops it. Israel's part is to repent and come back to the lost statutes and commandments.

precepts.text: The commandment was to speak unto the rock; Moses smote it twice, and because they believed not, to sanctify the Lord in the eyes of Israel, they did not bring the congregation into the land.
precepts.point: The reason is written: Moses rebelled against the commandment of the Most High in the desert of Zin at the water of Meribah. The Lord gave a specific commandment to speak unto the rock before their eyes, and Moses instead smote the rock twice; the water still came out abundantly, but Moses and Aaron did not sanctify the Lord in the eyes of the children of Israel, and for that neither of them brought the congregation into the land.

note.label: Numbers 27: The Daughters of Zelophehad and the Ordination of Joshua

precepts.why:
Moses would see the land from mount Abarim but not enter it, and be gathered unto his people as Aaron was, “For ye rebelled against my commandment in the desert of Zin, in the strife of the congregation, to sanctify me at the water before their eyes.” Here is that rebellion.

The Lord gave a specific commandment: “Take the rod, and gather thou the assembly together, thou, and Aaron thy brother, and speak ye unto the rock before their eyes; and it shall give forth his water.” Speak unto the rock. Instead Moses said, “Hear now, ye rebels; must we fetch you water out of this rock? And Moses lifted up his hand, and with his rod he smote the rock twice: and the water came out abundantly, and the congregation drank, and their beasts also.”

The water still came out abundantly, but the commandment was broken. “And the Lord spake unto Moses and Aaron, Because ye believed me not, to sanctify me in the eyes of the children of Israel, therefore ye shall not bring this congregation into the land which I have given them.” Moses and Aaron did not sanctify the Lord in the eyes of the children of Israel, and for that neither of them brought the congregation into the land.

precepts.text: The Lord said speak ye unto the rock; Moses smote it twice in anger, and because he believed not, to sanctify the Lord in the eyes of Israel, he could not bring the congregation into the land.
precepts.point: Moses is still good; he stood with Elias before Christ on the mount. He missed the promised land at that time, not the kingdom. But leadership carries the greater condemnation: the more given unto you, the more stripes when you fail.

note.label: Deuteronomy 1: The Second Giving of the Law

precepts.why:
“Also the Lord was angry with me for your sakes”: here is that history. At the waters the people fell into the same disbelief they had shown over and over, and the Lord told Moses, “Take the rod, and gather thou the assembly together, thou, and Aaron thy brother, and speak ye unto the rock before their eyes; and it shall give forth his water”. Speak to the rock.

Moses, in his anger, did not: “Hear now, ye rebels; must we fetch you water out of this rock? And Moses lifted up his hand, and with his rod he smote the rock twice”. He called them rebels and smote the rock twice when the Lord had said to speak to it. The water still came out abundantly, but the judgment followed: “Because ye believed me not, to sanctify me in the eyes of the children of Israel, therefore ye shall not bring this congregation into the land which I have given them.”

Moses failed to sanctify the Most High in the eyes of the children of Israel, and his judgment was to be kept out of the land: “Thou also shalt not go in thither.” It was for their sakes, their unbelief, that he was provoked; but the failure was his, and leadership carries the greater condemnation. The more given unto you, the more stripes when you fail.

precepts.text: Moses smote the rock twice and the water came out abundantly, but because he believed not, to sanctify the Most High in the eyes of the children of Israel, he and Aaron would not bring the congregation into the land.
precepts.point: The Lord was wroth with me for your sakes: Moses laid it on stiffnecked Israel. And the answer was final, let it suffice thee, speak no more unto me of this matter, as a parent tells a child that keeps begging that the matter is closed and had better not be raised again.

note.label: Deuteronomy 3: The Battle Is the Lord's

precepts.why:
“I pray thee, let me go over, and see the good land that is beyond Jordan”. The Most High had already told Moses he would not see the promised land, and here Moses is trying to get him to repent of the word he had given. The sentence came at the water of Meribah: “And Moses and Aaron gathered the congregation together before the rock, and he said unto them, Hear now, ye rebels; must we fetch you water out of this rock? And Moses lifted up his hand, and with his rod he smote the rock twice: and the water came out abundantly”.

Must we fetch you water: Moses took the credit and became high minded, instead of sanctifying the Most High in the eyes of the children of Israel. So the word came: “Because ye believed me not, to sanctify me in the eyes of the children of Israel, therefore ye shall not bring this congregation into the land which I have given them.” The contrast is Deuteronomy 3:3: after the war with Og the people said the Lord our God delivered them into our hands. That is sanctifying the Most High. Moses at the rock did the opposite.

“But the Lord was wroth with me for your sakes”: Moses laid it on stiffnecked Israel, the rebels who provoked him at the rock. And the answer was final: “Let it suffice thee; speak no more unto me of this matter.” As a parent tells a child that keeps begging that the matter is closed and had better not be raised again, the Most High closed it.

precepts.text: Edom refused to give Israel passage through his border, just as Jephthah rehearsed it.
precepts.point: And the LORD God of Israel delivered Sihon and all his people into the hand of Israel, and they smote them: so Israel possessed all the land of the Amorites, from Arnon even unto Jabbok, and from the wilderness even unto Jordan. That is how Israel got the land of the Amorites: the Lord gave it in battle when they came out against his people.

note.label: Judges 11: Jephthah and the Search of the Fathers

precepts.why: Jephthah said Israel “sent messengers unto the king of Edom, saying, Let me, I pray thee, pass through thy land: but the king of Edom would not hearken thereto.” The record in Numbers says the same: “Thus Edom refused to give Israel passage through his border: wherefore Israel turned away from him.” Just as Jephthah rehearsed it: Israel asked passage, Edom refused, and Israel turned away and compassed the land of Edom rather than force a way through. Israel took nobody’s land on that journey until Sihon came out against them.
